I was terrified of pressing publish. My first podcast sat in a folder for thirty days.
Every night I fixed a tiny breath, convinced that someone would hear it and laugh.
Then I realized the person I was editing for didn't exist. My sister just wanted to hear the story.
I finally sent her the rough cut. She called back before the credits finished.
On the second episode I tried a different experiment with the opening.
What if the most interesting question comes halfway through the conversation?
I moved the question to the first ten seconds, then kept the long silence before the answer.
Because of that pause, you can actually hear the guest deciding to tell the truth.
In the third interview our recorder failed. We lost almost the whole afternoon.
I was afraid to ask our guest to start again. She had already given us so much.
But the second time she skipped the rehearsed answer and told us why she left.
We saved six minutes. Those six minutes became the entire episode.
People ask how I know when a story is finished. I used to count the edits.
Now I listen for the sentence I would repeat to a friend on the walk home.
I learned that a good ending gives someone else a place to begin.
